newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Sept CPI seen down 0.1 pct,up 1.4 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: German Sept CPI seen down 0.1 pct,up 1.4 pct yr/yr.

text.p: West German inflation is likely to have stayed tame in September and will remain at annual rates of 1.4 percent to 1.5 percent for the rest of the year, economists predicted on Monday.
Consumer price figures from four west German states will be released from Tuesday and will be used to calculate preliminary data for west Germany, due on Thursday or Friday.

Economists on average expect the west German data to show consumer prices down 0.1 percent month-on-month and up 1.4 percent year-on-year, the same as the August rates for both west German and pan-German consumer prices.
The Federal Statistics Office provides preliminary inflation data only for west Germany. Final west German data will be published along with pan-German inflation next month.
"Overall we expect the price climate to remain favourable for the rest of the year," said Thomas Kull, an economist at WestLB in Duesseldorf. "Inflation will remain unchanged, it won't fall further."
Economists said a sharp fall in the price of travel services like package holidays compared with the holiday month of August had partly offset an increase in oil prices during September.
"If you look at the leading indicators there's no sign of inflationary pressure," said Armin Kayser, an economist at Swiss Bank Corp in Frankfurt.
The benign inflation picture was borne out by German August import prices released on Monday which showed declines of 0.2 percent month-on-month and 0.3 percent year-on-year.
August producer prices released last Friday were flat month-on-month and down 0.7 percent year-on-year.
The states of Baden-Wuerttemberg and North Rhine-Westphalia said they would probably release their consumer price data on Tuesday. Hesse said it would do so Tuesday morning or Wednesday morning.
Bavaria said it had no fixed date yet but expected to issue its figures mid-week.
